title: Common-reference presentation of finite AC f-divergence
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Theorem 8.3.1 proof, printed p. 219 / PDF p. 230: identify nu with a density q relative to a common reference measure m, then write the f-divergence integral as integral q f(rho) dm, with rho representing dmu/dnu.
target_statement: For the finite absolutely-continuous f-divergence child and a denominator law nu=m.withDensity q, rewrite its measure-facing integral as integral q.toReal * f(rho) dm whenever rho agrees nu-a.e. with Samplinglib's canonical real RN density. Reuse Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀; do not reprove integration against withDensity or the RN quotient identity.
parents: ASTIS-SW-common-reference-rn-real-density (later discharges the rho parent contract for two common-reference laws)

searched: Pinned Mathlib v4.33.0: MeasureTheory.integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ exactly rewrites Bochner integration against an ENNReal density to integration of its real scalar multiple
Samplinglib finite AC f-divergence child #231 provides the measure-facing value and density-representative invariance
Samplinglib common-reference RN real-density child #229 provides the canonical p/q realization when both laws are withDensity measures
No Samplinglib theorem already joins these three interfaces
shared_floor_audit.notes: This is intentionally a representation adapter. It takes the RN-density equality as a parent contract rather than importing/reproving #229 on this parallel branch. The only new source-shaped statement is that the finite measure-level divergence equals the weighted common-reference integral used by Theorem 8.3.1. Density measurability and a.e. finiteness are exactly the hypotheses of the reused pinned-Mathlib withDensity integral theorem.
